params.place: on the map: the political world map

moments.what: a passport lands on the world map
pins pop up on every continent
the camera pulls back to the whole world, the flags fold down
an eraser sweeps the borders away, the colours melt into one
one colour covers every continent

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: What if one passport worked everywhere, because Earth was one country?

params.place: on the map: flags planted on every continent

moments.what: a moon crosses the sky over the map
flags pop up on country after country, a counter on a board
the UN board stamps on
the flags lean toward each other
every flag slides down its pole
one white flag rises in the middle of the map
the new flag waves
the camera pulls back over the whole planet

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Overnight, all 193 members of the United Nations become one, and every flag comes down for a single new one, flying over the whole planet.

params.place: on the map: crowds on every continent

moments.what: little people appear on every continent
the camera drifts over the whole world
each holds up a passport
all the passports turn one colour
a name writes onto a big passport
the big passport's cover stamps shut
a VISA tag is torn off

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Every person on the planet now carries that same passport: the same colour, the same name on the cover, and nobody needs a visa again.

params.place: on the map: the road from Lisbon to Singapore

moments.what: lines of trucks wait at a border gate
the gate and the queue vanish in a puff
a truck sets off
a pin drops on Lisbon
the route draws across Asia to a pin on Singapore
Europe and Asia flash as the route crosses them
a stamp falls, crossed out

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Border queues vanish overnight. A truck leaves Lisbon and drives all the way to Singapore, across two continents, without a single stamp.

params.place: on the map: a bank vault drawn over the oceans

moments.what: a pile of notes lands on the map
a rupee note lands on India
a dollar note lands on America
a euro note lands on Europe
a yen note lands on Japan
the currencies count up on a board
the notes melt and swirl together
one gold coin spins up in the middle

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then the money: rupees, dollars, euros, yen. About 180 currencies melt into one coin.

params.place: on the map: the world's capitals

moments.what: pins glow on capital cities
a crown hovers over the map
more capitals light up
the pins jump and wave
the crown spins, undecided
Washington's pin jumps
Delhi's pin jumps
Beijing's pin jumps
speech bubbles pop over the three pins
the crown swings between them

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So which city becomes the capital? Every capital on the map wants the job, from Washington to Delhi to Beijing, and every one of them says it should win.

params.place: on the map: the countries that drive on the left

moments.what: the map flips to evening light
a big road sign drops on the map
the map glows one colour
the cars settle on the right
Britain lights up, a car on the left
India lights up
Japan lights up
an arrow points left on each
cars fill the roads
the cars swerve across to the right

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Here's the catch: one country means one set of road rules. Britain, India and Japan drive on the left, so millions of drivers switch sides overnight.

params.place: on the map: day and night across the world

moments.what: a big clock stands on the map
the day line sweeps across the map
the sun sinks toward the horizon
the sun sets over Tokyo
London sits in the dark
a little man in London sits up in bed and stretches
the clock wobbles
time zone stripes draw down the map

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And one country still can't share one clock: the sun sets over Tokyo just as London wakes up, so the time zones all stay.

params.place: on the map: the one-country world

moments.what: the camera pushes in on a traveller with a suitcase
the last dotted line rubs out
a FOREIGN label is crossed out
the airport sign flips
a plane takes off
a pin drops on Paris
a pin drops on Peru
it lands on a HOME sign

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: But the strangest part: with every border gone, there is no foreign country left. Every trip abroad, from Paris to Peru, becomes a trip at home.

params.place: on the map: the world, borders drawn back

moments.what: a passport pops up on the left
a fan of flags pops up on the right
the world map sits between them
a question mark bounces
a comment bubble pops up
the borders draw back on: the first frame

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: One passport, or 193 flags: which world would you pick? Tell me in the comments. And picture it again:
